artifacts.title: Psiaki v. Pacific Northwest Presbytery

matches.evidence: 2023-11 — Psiaki v. Pacific Northwest Presbytery Court: Standing Judicial Commission · Assembly: 51st (2024) · Disposition: sustained Source: [ga51_2024 pp. 867–909](../markdown/ga51_2024.md ga51-p86

> Question: That the Presbytery ask the General Assembly's Permanent Committee on Judicial Business if a congregation may be permitted to set a minimum age for voting in view of BCO 6- 2, 6-4, 24-3, 25-1 and 25-3.

artifacts.synopsis: Mr. Psiaki complained that Covenant Presbyterian Church's Session erred in installing officers elected at a congregational meeting that excluded communicant members under age 18 from voting, in violation of the BCO. The SJC sustained the complaint (15-5), holding that all communicant members have a constitutional right to vote in officer elections regardless of age, and that church bylaws may not override BCO provisions; multiple dissenting opinions argued that BCO 20-3 and 24-3's phrase 'good and regular standing' permits local sessions to establish reasonable minimum voting ages.

artifacts.title: Whether a session may set a minimum age for communicant membership

matches.evidence: The CCB advised that sessions must evaluate each membership request individually regardless of age, since the timing of credible faith cannot be precisely fixed.

artifacts.title: Whether congregation may set minimum voting age for elections

matches.evidence: The BCO provides no minimum voting age for congregational meetings, except where state law imposes one for corporate votes.

artifacts.title: Sufficiency of faith profession for visible church membership

matches.evidence: CCB found proposed overtures conflicting with BCO because the only required profession for church membership is faith in Jesus Christ, with the session judging qualifications.
